variants.name: Typed AbortSignal through options objects
variants.idiom_name: readonly AbortSignal in an options parameter, narrowed with throwIfAborted()
variants.implementation_notes: TypeScript does not add cancellation semantics, it types the platform's: AbortSignal comes from lib.dom.d.ts or @types/node, so the tsconfig lib setting decides whether the type exists at all, and the idiomatic shape is an options object with an optional readonly signal that every function forwards. signal.throwIfAborted() doubles as a check and a narrowing point (it throws a DOMException), while keeping signal as AbortSignal rather than a hand-written { aborted: boolean } makes the platform's composition helpers (timeout, any) assignable to the same parameters. Where no platform API exists, model the token as an interface with readonly aborted plus a subscribe method, but keep the abort signal at the boundary and translate once.
pitfalls: Without DOM (or @types/node) in the tsconfig lib, AbortSignal is not in scope and the mistake shows up as a compile error or a silent any depending on settings - a build-time false negative for cancellation code.

Structural typing accepts any object with an aborted property where an AbortSignal is expected: keep the parameter type exact, or a custom pseudo-token will bind where composition helpers are required.
With strictNullChecks off, signal?.aborted checks lose their meaning and a missing signal passes unnoticed; cancellation code is one of the places where strict mode is not optional.
TypeScript erases at compile time: every check must exist in the emitted JavaScript, so a typed token interface cannot be the only carrier of the request.

variants.name: Typed signal composition for deadlines
variants.implementation_notes: The composition variant is the same runtime feature set as JavaScript with a typed seam: a helper takes the caller's AbortSignal and a duration and returns a composed signal, so components expose one cancellation parameter while still enforcing their own deadline. Type the reason as unknown and narrow it deliberately (DOMException with name TimeoutError for timeouts), and keep the composition inside the component so callers do not manage linked controllers. Under target/lib settings without these static methods, fall back to a controller plus a timer and forward the same typed signal.
pitfalls: The lib/target combination gates the static methods: with older libs AbortSignal.timeout/any do not exist in the types even when the runtime has them, so the fallback path must be maintained and typed too.
Narrowing signal.reason needs a runtime check (instanceof DOMException plus name), because the type of reason is unknown and a cast hides the difference between a timeout and a caller abort.
